key_concepts: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell
Multicellular organisms are made up of many specialized cells
Prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus and contain a nucleoid
Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells share DNA as a component
Multicellularity allows specialized functions and increased complexity
Multicellular organisms can replace or repair damaged cells, supporting longer lifespans
Bacteria and Euglena are examples of unicellular organisms
Humans, dogs, and mushrooms are examples of multicellular or eukaryotic organisms
Overall cell size is restricted by the need to transport materials inside the cell
